change: Document validation reuses one private bounded NodePathCursor. Only retained validation issues and first entity-ID occurrences snapshot an immutable NodePath. Every recursive return pops its index before the next sibling. No node validation, schema rule, limit, error ordering or wire contract is skipped or changed.
tests: New retained-path sibling/depth-cutoff regression passed before the runtime change (1122 other library tests filtered). It checks duplicate-identity first paths and exact cutoff paths after traversal returns to later siblings.
All-feature core library: 1124 passed, including cursor snapshots across all 256 depths, failed extension preserving the cursor, root pop and reuse without modifying retained snapshots.
Strict all-feature/all-target core Clippy and cargo fmt --check passed.
14 generated ABI/declaration tests, strict TypeScript, Node heading compatibility and Node list command/projection/recovery checks passed.
Five raw-Wasm runs each in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit passed.
Five full DOM/router/controller/toolbar/queue/adapter/IndexedDB/recovery runs each in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit passed.
Private installed consumers passed in all three engines; unchanged base Node/TypeScript/Chromium consumer smoke passed. Shipping trees verified unchanged by the pack checker.

measurements.method: Unchanged installed-package fixtures, sequential old/new/old/new core measurements followed by old/new full-browser measurements. Three independent cases at each of 10/100/500 items in each engine. No timeout or assertion was relaxed. All six reports reached measured after their correctness checks: 162 cases total.
measurements.reportResolution: Report paths are relative to the corresponding artifact consumer directory above.
measurements.interpretation: Repeatable local reduction in core post-edit preparation across both alternating pairs. Full-editor medians also decreased in this single pair; WebKit ranges overlap. Not a p95, human input, multi-device or release-latency claim. Firefox 500-item edits remain slow.

limits: The initial cargo command was unavailable on PATH; the installed /Users/s/.cargo/bin/cargo was used. Its unscoped filtered baseline command continued launching unrelated zero-test integration binaries; those are not claimed as integration coverage or a quiet-machine baseline.
A read-only host CPU snapshot was denied by the sandbox. No background processes were stopped; an idle machine is not claimed.
Native Safari/Chrome evidence from earlier checkpoints belongs to the previous Wasm hash; it is not silently relabeled as native qualification of this candidate.
Size ceilings, optional delivery policy, IME, screen-reader qualification, prior intermittent faults/timeouts and the full release gate remain open.
